source.title: Geometric Limits of Knowledge Distillation: A Minimum-Width Theorem via Superposition Theory

page_placements.theme: Representation-level evidence of sparse, overcomplete feature structure in real models

record.tranche_reason: Tests the feature-capacity mechanism associated with superposition using SAE measurements and toy-network distillation outcomes, rather than measuring mixed responses of individual neurons.
record.gate_note: The study measures feature count, sparsity, and a capacity threshold; it does not test whether individual neurons respond to unrelated input kinds. The distillation-loss floors and linear-probe results concern consequences of compression, not neuron-level polysemanticity, so they are not recorded as rows for these claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study takes superposition as given and uses it to predict knowledge-distillation loss floors. Its toy-model result checks the accuracy of its own floor formula. Its Pythia-410M result counts SAE features in the residual stream against residual width. Neither measures whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs, or whether superposition causes such mixed responses. No row bears on any version as stated.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors argue the distillation floor has two parts: a geometric, width-dependent term from student capacity under superposition, and a width-independent architectural baseline B (affine fit R² = 0.993). They report that Pythia-410M's SAE-measured critical width is about 1,065, above 1,024, and that coarse concepts survive 81x compression in linear probes.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SAE feature counts and sparsity, compressed-sensing capacity calculations, and distillation-floor comparisons; it does not use neuron activation maximization or inspect unrelated input examples for individual neurons.
record.method_sensitivity: Toy-model floor predictions vary with α and student width. Pythia SAE measurements vary by layer (d*S ranges from 1,065 to 1,186); the authors describe the threshold as robust to layer choice.

fits_no_version.finding: SAEs with 32x expansion on the Pythia-410M residual stream find about 28.7k–31k alive features at α ≈ 0.992. The derived critical width d*S of 1,065–1,186 exceeds the residual width of 1,024 at layers 8, 12 and 16.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Language-model residual streams contain more sparse SAE features than dimensions (representation-level superposition), measured via SAE feature counts.

record.problems: The evidence is indirect for neuron polysemanticity: SAE feature counts and a derived capacity threshold do not show that individual neurons encode unrelated features or that this causes mixed responses. The real-model evidence is from one model, and the authors note that their theorem assumes an approximately random-projection bottleneck and that the multilayer extension is empirically validated rather than proven.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for the five student KL floors or linear-probe accuracies: those measure compression loss and coarse-concept decodability, not the neuron-level mixed responses or feature packing named by the versions.

untested.parts: No neuron-level analysis of MLP neurons in language models.
Assumes superposition but never links neuron polysemanticity to feature count. The SAE results concern residual-stream dimensions, not neurons.
No comparison of activation functions, architectures or regularization for their effect on polysemantic neurons.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' with a V3 'supports' label is overturned. The paper concerns distillation limits and treats superposition as an assumption, citing Elhage et al. and Scherlis et al. The SAE feature counts depend on the chosen dictionary size. The paper also gives inconsistent L0 values for layer 8 (about 7,400 in the text versus 234.9 in Table 1).

versions.untested_parts: No image classifier or vision-neuron responses are measured.
No comparison of MLP neurons responding to unrelated tokens or contexts in language models.
Measures feature surplus and sparsity, but does not directly establish that individual neurons pack unrelated features or that this causes their mixed responses.
No test of polysemanticity arising from initialization, regularization, or training noise when capacity is sufficient.
No comparison of activation functions, architectures, or regularization for their effect on the share of polysemantic neurons.
No analysis of whether apparently polysemantic neurons have a shared feature or related jobs.
No comparison of activation ranges or explanation-scoring methods for classifying neurons as polysemantic.

rows.subject: Elhage et al. [2022] single-layer autoencoder
rows.stage_stated: students trained at dS = 1, . . . , dT; 20 seeds
rows.operation_detail: Compared actual distillation floors with the capacity-based formula across toy-model configurations.

conditions.value: 48 combinations of n, dT, and α

rows.measure: Refined g(α)-aware formula prediction versus actual floor; Pearson r = 0.93 and MAPE = 93.9%.
rows.baseline: Actual floors; a numerical baseline value is not stated.
rows.uncertainty: Actual floors shown as mean ±1 std across 20 seeds; numerical uncertainty for the aggregate metrics is not stated.
rows.note: Reported as an aggregate across 48 configurations and 140 data points. The authors say the refined formula closely tracks actual floors and captures the critical width.
rows.check: This is the study's own distillation-floor formula evaluated against actual student floors in the toy autoencoder, i.e. method performance. It measures no neuron polysemanticity and no cause of it. Also, a MAPE of 93.9% is a large error, not a good fit; the authors explain it as systematic overestimation of absolute floors.

rows.subject: Pythia-410M
rows.operation_detail: Trained SAEs and measured alive features, activation sparsity, and derived feature capacity at layer 8.
rows.measure: Alive feature count, average L0, α, g(α), and critical student width d*S.
rows.note: The derived critical width exceeds teacher width.
rows.check: Residual-stream SAE statistics at layer 8, not MLP neurons, so it does not bear on V3's neuron-level mechanism. The alive-feature count is bounded by the chosen 32x dictionary size, so F > d partly reflects that choice. The text also says layer 8 has L0 ≈ 7,400, which conflicts with Table 1's 234.9; the value is unreliable.

relation.reason: Superposition is a premise of Theorem 1. The study never examines individual neurons or whether they respond to unrelated inputs.

tranche.reason: Takes superposition as given to predict distillation loss floors and reports its own formula's accuracy. Its SAE counts are residual-stream features vs width, not neuron polysemanticity.

source_check.notes: Residual-stream SAE counts at 32x, capped by the 32,768-feature dictionary; not MLP neurons. The paper is internally inconsistent: §5.1 gives layer-8 L0 of about 7,400 and 15-40% feature death at layers 12/16, but Table 1 gives L0 234.9 and about 11-13% dead. Rows follow Table 1.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Toy-model configurations and measured Pythia-410M layers 8, 12, and 16
reader_labels.reason: The formula tracks toy-model floors across the reported configurations, and each Pythia layer has a derived feature-capacity threshold above the 1024-wide teacher; these results support the capacity/superposition account, but do not demonstrate mixed responses of individual neurons (R1–R4).
